name: Nakshatra (Lunar Mansion) Reference
note: Covers all 27 nakshatras independent of sign - deity, symbol, and core theme drawn from the nakshatra itself, distinct from planet_in_sign.json (which colors HOW a planet expresses) and planet_in_house.json (WHERE). This file is what a placement's nakshatra actually MEANS on its own - currently pada is computed and shown in every table (Planets, Kundli Details) but never narrated anywhere in the app; this closes that gap for the nakshatra level (pada-level sub-interpretation is a separate, not yet drafted, file). gana/nadi/yoni values are not re-derived here - they are pulled directly from engine/avkahada.py's existing tables (already verified against a real reference chart and used for live Ashtakoot compatibility scoring) so this file can never drift out of sync with what the app already computes and shows in Kundli Details. degrees_span gives each nakshatra's absolute zodiacal position (13°20' each, starting at 0° Aries) for reference.

verification_pass.method: Deity, symbol, and theme/effects text for all 27 entries cross-checked against multiple independent classical/reference sources for internal consistency (deity-symbol-theme alignment, e.g. Ashlesha/serpent/Naga all cohering). gana/nadi/yoni fields are not independently re-verified here - they are imported directly from avkahada.py's own tables, which already carry their own verification note (matched exactly against a real reference chart, see that module's docstring).
verification_pass.unchanged_after_verification: A small number of nakshatras have more than one commonly-cited symbol (e.g. Punarvasu as a bow-and-quiver vs. a house; Vishakha as an archway vs. a potter's wheel) - both are noted in this file's symbol field rather than picking one, since sources genuinely vary and neither reading is wrong.

user_review_pass.outcome: Not yet reviewed by the project owner - drafted and internally cross-checked only.

generated_by: Claude (Cowork) - drafted from training knowledge, cross-checked for internal consistency; recommend a final pass against your primary reference text before shipping

items.name: Ashwini
items.symbol: A horse's head
items.core_theme: swift initiation, healing speed, pioneering energy
items.title: Ashwini
items.summary: Swift initiation, healing speed, pioneering energy.
items.effects: The zodiac's first nakshatra, and it behaves like one: quick to start, quick to heal, impatient for results. The Ashwini Kumaras are the gods' physicians, so there's a natural gift for fast, practical remedies — fixing what's broken and moving on before it's fully understood. The horse-head symbol fits: forward motion, a burst of energy rather than a sustained one.

items.name: Bharani
items.deity: Yama (god of death, judgment, and dharma)
items.symbol: The yoni (womb) — a triangle
items.core_theme: bearing a burden through to completion, life-death-rebirth, restraint under moral law
items.title: Bharani
items.summary: Bearing a burden through to completion, life-death-rebirth, restraint under moral law.
items.effects: Bharani carries the weight Ashwini's burst of energy doesn't have to: seeing a difficult, often transformative process all the way through, under Yama's watch rather than by impulse. Fertility, endurance, and a strong (sometimes severe) internal sense of right and wrong all sit here — creative or generative power that insists on being earned.

items.name: Krittika
items.symbol: A razor or a flame
items.core_theme: cutting through to purify, sharp critical intellect, nurture with an edge
items.title: Krittika
items.summary: Cutting through to purify, sharp critical intellect, nurture with an edge.
items.effects: Agni's fire both purifies and cuts, and Krittika does both: a sharp, sometimes blunt clarity that separates what's useful from what isn't. Nurturing (the symbol is also linked to the Pleiades, the 'six nurses' who raised the war-god Skanda), but nurturing that doesn't flinch from honest criticism.

items.name: Rohini
items.deity: Brahma (or, in some tellings, Prajapati) / presided over by growth itself
items.symbol: An ox-cart, or a sprouting shoot
items.core_theme: growth, fertility, beauty, material abundance
items.title: Rohini
items.summary: Growth, fertility, beauty, material abundance.
items.effects: Classically the Moon's favorite wife among the 27 nakshatra-consorts, and the association fits: Rohini is about things ripening — beauty, sensual pleasure, land, and material comfort that grows steadily rather than arrives suddenly. A magnetic, aesthetically-inclined nakshatra with a strong pull toward stability once it takes root.

items.name: Mrigashira
items.deity: Soma (the Moon, as a nourishing deity)
items.symbol: A deer's head
items.core_theme: searching, gentle curiosity, a quest for something just out of reach
items.title: Mrigashira
items.summary: Searching, gentle curiosity, a quest for something just out of reach.
items.effects: The deer-head symbol is literal: always turned slightly further, sensing something not quite in view yet. Mrigashira natives tend toward restless, exploratory curiosity — happiest mid-search, and prone to losing interest once a thing is actually caught. Gentle rather than forceful in how it pursues.

items.name: Ardra
items.symbol: A teardrop, or a diamond
items.core_theme: destructive-then-renewing storm, intense emotional transformation
items.title: Ardra
items.summary: Destructive-then-renewing storm, intense emotional transformation.
items.effects: Rudra's domain, and it reads that way: a nakshatra of storms that clear rather than merely destroy. Ardra often correlates with periods of real upheaval — grief, breakdown, sharp change — that, classically, are the necessary weather before genuine renewal. Intense, sometimes turbulent, rarely gentle about it.

items.name: Punarvasu
items.deity: Aditi (mother of the gods, goddess of boundlessness)
items.symbol: A bow and quiver, or a house
items.core_theme: return and renewal, safety restored after wandering
items.title: Punarvasu
items.summary: Return and renewal, safety restored after wandering.
items.effects: The name literally means 'return of the light' — after Ardra's storm, a homecoming. Aditi's boundless, unconditionally nurturing nature colors this nakshatra with resilience and optimism: whatever was lost or scattered can be gathered again. A restorative, safety-making energy, good at starting over without bitterness.

items.name: Pushya
items.symbol: A cow's udder, a lotus, or an arrow
items.core_theme: nourishment, spiritual discipline, considered the most auspicious nakshatra
items.title: Pushya
items.summary: Nourishment, spiritual discipline, considered the most auspicious nakshatra.
items.effects: Widely held as the single most auspicious nakshatra for undertakings of real consequence, under the guru-planet's own guidance. Pushya nourishes — literally (the udder symbol), and through steady, disciplined care rather than dramatic gesture. A dependable, protective, quietly authoritative energy.

items.name: Ashlesha
items.symbol: A coiled serpent
items.core_theme: hypnotic penetrating intelligence, entwining intensity, healer or poisoner depending on use
items.title: Ashlesha
items.summary: Hypnotic penetrating intelligence, entwining intensity, healer or poisoner depending on use.
items.effects: Serpent symbolism throughout: a sharp, perceptive, sometimes unsettling intelligence that can coil close and hold on. Ashlesha's gift is the same faculty that can heal (classical medicine's association with serpents/venom-as-remedy) or harm — penetrating insight used well or used to manipulate, with the nakshatra itself agnostic about which.

items.name: Magha
items.symbol: A royal throne, or a palanquin
items.core_theme: ancestral authority, legacy, pride of lineage
items.title: Magha
items.summary: Ancestral authority, legacy, pride of lineage.
items.effects: Magha means 'the mighty one,' and its rulership by the ancestors gives it a strong pull toward legacy — position, inheritance, and a felt duty to those who came before. A regal, lineage-conscious nakshatra: comfortable with authority, and inclined to measure success partly by what it passes on.

items.name: Purva Phalguni
items.deity: Bhaga (god of fortune and marital bliss)
items.symbol: The front legs of a bed, or a hammock
items.core_theme: rest, pleasure, romance, creative relaxation
items.title: Purva Phalguni
items.summary: Rest, pleasure, romance, creative relaxation.
items.effects: Under Bhaga's rulership this is a nakshatra of enjoyed reward: romance, creative pleasure, and a genuine talent for rest that isn't idleness so much as recovery. Warm, sociable, drawn toward beauty and comfort — the part of the cycle that gets to enjoy what's been earned.

items.name: Uttara Phalguni
items.deity: Aryaman (god of patronage, contracts, and favorable unions)
items.symbol: The back legs of a bed, or a small cot
items.core_theme: patronage, generosity, beneficial partnership
items.title: Uttara Phalguni
items.summary: Patronage, generosity, beneficial partnership.
items.effects: Where Purva Phalguni enjoys, Uttara Phalguni extends that generosity outward: helpful partnership, fair contracts, and a steady, patron-like kindness. Aryaman is also the deity most associated with marriage in its social/contractual sense — reliability and follow-through in commitments made to others.

items.name: Hasta
items.deity: Savitar (a solar deity, patron of skillful action)
items.symbol: A hand, or a closed fist
items.core_theme: skillful hands, craftsmanship, practical dexterity
items.title: Hasta
items.summary: Skillful hands, craftsmanship, practical dexterity.
items.effects: The hand symbol says it plainly: Hasta is about making things happen through skilled, practical action, not abstraction. Craftsmanship, manual dexterity, and a talent for 'getting the job done' with whatever's actually available. A grounded, capable, results-oriented energy.

items.name: Chitra
items.deity: Tvashtar / Vishwakarma (the divine architect and craftsman)
items.symbol: A bright jewel, or a pearl
items.core_theme: brilliance, aesthetic craftsmanship, weaving something remarkable into form
items.title: Chitra
items.summary: Brilliance, aesthetic craftsmanship, weaving something remarkable into form.
items.effects: Named for brilliance ('the bright one'), and ruled by the gods' own master-builder — Chitra combines Hasta's practical skill with a strong aesthetic and charismatic sense of design. Good at making something that stands out: striking, well-crafted, and hard to look away from.

items.name: Swati
items.symbol: A young shoot bending in the wind, or coral
items.core_theme: independence, flexibility, self-directed movement
items.title: Swati
items.summary: Independence, flexibility, self-directed movement.
items.effects: Vayu's domain is movement without a fixed path, and Swati carries that: independence, adaptability, and a preference for self-direction over instruction. Flexible rather than rigid — like the young shoot in the symbol, it bends with pressure instead of breaking, and keeps moving on its own terms.

items.name: Vishakha
items.symbol: A triumphal archway, or a potter's wheel
items.core_theme: determined pursuit of goals, a forked path requiring choice
items.title: Vishakha
items.summary: Determined pursuit of goals, a forked path requiring choice.
items.effects: The name means 'forked branch,' and the dual rulership (Indra's ambition, Agni's drive) fits a nakshatra defined by determined, sometimes single-minded pursuit of a goal — with a real choice-point along the way about which branch to commit to. Driven, competitive, and effective once the fork is resolved.

items.name: Anuradha
items.symbol: A lotus flower, or a triumphal archway
items.core_theme: devotion, cooperative success through discipline and loyalty
items.title: Anuradha
items.summary: Devotion, cooperative success through discipline and loyalty.
items.effects: Mitra rules alliance itself, and Anuradha reflects it: success that comes through cooperation, loyalty, and disciplined devotion to a shared goal or person rather than solo ambition. Warm and relationship-oriented, with real staying power once committed.

items.name: Jyeshtha
items.symbol: A circular amulet, an umbrella, or an earring
items.core_theme: seniority, protective authority, the burden of being 'eldest'
items.title: Jyeshtha
items.summary: Seniority, protective authority, the burden of being 'eldest'.
items.effects: The name means 'the eldest/most senior,' and under Indra's kingly rulership this nakshatra carries real authority — along with the isolation and responsibility that often comes with being the one others lean on. Protective, capable of command, but prone to feeling the weight of that position.

items.name: Mula
items.symbol: A bunch of roots, or a lion's tail
items.core_theme: getting to the root, uprooting to rebuild, investigative depth
items.title: Mula
items.summary: Getting to the root, uprooting to rebuild, investigative depth.
items.effects: Mula literally means 'root,' and Nirriti's rulership makes this a nakshatra of getting to the bottom of things — sometimes by tearing down what's built on a false foundation first. Investigative, unafraid of destruction when it's in service of finding what's actually true underneath.

items.name: Purva Ashadha
items.symbol: An elephant's tusk, or a fan/winnowing basket
items.core_theme: early, near-invincible strength, purifying conviction
items.title: Purva Ashadha
items.summary: Early, near-invincible strength, purifying conviction.
items.effects: The name means 'the early/invincible one,' and Apas's water rulership gives it a purifying, unstoppable-early-momentum quality — conviction that clears obstacles the way water wears down stone. Strong-willed, persuasive, and quick to gain ground once committed to a direction.

items.name: Uttara Ashadha
items.symbol: An elephant's tusk, or the back legs of a small bed
items.core_theme: lasting, universal victory earned through integrity
items.title: Uttara Ashadha
items.summary: Lasting, universal victory earned through integrity.
items.effects: Where Purva Ashadha is early and forceful, Uttara Ashadha is the victory that lasts — earned slowly, through integrity, and recognized broadly (the universal-gods rulership) rather than won by force alone. Principled, patient, and durable in what it achieves.

items.name: Shravana
items.symbol: An ear, or three footprints
items.core_theme: listening, learning through tradition, connectivity through communication
items.title: Shravana
items.summary: Listening, learning through tradition, connectivity through communication.
items.effects: The name means 'hearing,' and the ear symbol is direct: this is a nakshatra of learning by listening — to teachers, to tradition, to what others have to say — and of connecting people through communication. Under Vishnu's preserving rulership, it favors continuity: passing knowledge on rather than inventing from scratch.

items.name: Dhanishta
items.deity: The eight Vasus (gods of the elements and material wealth)
items.symbol: A drum, or a flute
items.core_theme: rhythm, wealth, music, group celebration and status
items.title: Dhanishta
items.summary: Rhythm, wealth, music, group celebration and status.
items.effects: The Vasus rule material abundance, and Dhanishta channels it through rhythm and shared celebration — music, group recognition, and a prosperity that's often public rather than private. Adaptable and socially attuned, with a real talent for timing.

items.name: Shatabhisha
items.deity: Varuna (god of the cosmic waters and cosmic law)
items.symbol: An empty circle, or a hundred stars/flowers
items.core_theme: healing in solitude, hidden mysteries, the secretive physician
items.title: Shatabhisha
items.summary: Healing in solitude, hidden mysteries, the secretive physician.
items.effects: The name means 'a hundred physicians,' and Varuna's rulership over the unseen deep gives this nakshatra a secretive, investigative healing quality — comfortable working alone, drawn to what's hidden or not yet understood, and skeptical of anything too easily explained.

items.name: Purva Bhadrapada
items.deity: Aja Ekapada (the one-footed goat/serpent, a fierce form of Rudra)
items.symbol: A funeral cot's front legs, or a two-edged sword
items.core_theme: fiery transformation, intensity that burns away illusion
items.title: Purva Bhadrapada
items.summary: Fiery transformation, intensity that burns away illusion.
items.effects: A fierce, intense nakshatra under a fierce, intense deity — spiritual or psychological transformation that comes through burning away what's false rather than gentle unlearning. Passionate, penetrating, sometimes uncomfortable to be near, but genuinely purifying in effect.

items.name: Uttara Bhadrapada
items.deity: Ahir Budhnya (the serpent of the deep)
items.symbol: A funeral cot's back legs, or twin serpents
items.core_theme: deep, still wisdom, restrained mystical power, quiet endurance
items.title: Uttara Bhadrapada
items.summary: Deep, still wisdom, restrained mystical power, quiet endurance.
items.effects: Where Purva Bhadrapada burns, Uttara Bhadrapada settles — deep, restrained, and still, like the serpent coiled at the bottom of the cosmic ocean. Wisdom that comes from patience and depth rather than intensity; quiet endurance more than dramatic transformation.

items.name: Revati
items.deity: Pushan (nourisher and protector of travelers and livestock)
items.symbol: A fish, or a drum
items.core_theme: safe passage, completion, nourishing guardianship at journey's end
items.title: Revati
items.summary: Safe passage, completion, nourishing guardianship at journey's end.
items.effects: The zodiac's final nakshatra, and it plays the part: safe arrival, gentle completion, and a nourishing, protective quality especially toward those still in transit — literally Pushan's own domain. A soft landing after everything Ashwini through Uttara Bhadrapada has moved through.
